content.value: Sequential search scans entries and can work on unsorted data. Return a matching index or a documented sentinel such as -1. Stop early when appropriate. Binary search requires sorted data and repeatedly compares the target with the midpoint, discarding one half. Duplicate values may have multiple valid matching positions.

For [8, 3, 6] and target 3, index becomes 1 after two comparisons. For target 5, the result remains -1. Sequential search may inspect every element, while binary search reduces its candidate range by roughly half per step.
Practice: trace the example by hand, change one input, and explain how the result changes. Check an empty or boundary case when the preconditions allow it.
